reason: Lending collateral valued off a same-block price the borrower can set (self-trade/spot/cheap oracle), then borrowed and withdrawn against with flash-loan capital.
Attacker cheaply acquires a voting quorum, passes a malicious proposal, and uses the resulting admin/upgrade/mint power to drain protocol funds.
Balancer BPool-family single-asset join/exit math and rounding against a dust reserve mints shares (or extracts value) without proportional input.
Bonding-curve / internal-pricing redemptions that are not path-independent, so repeatedly stepping through the curve in small operations pays out more than a lump sum.
Unsafe narrowing cast / integer wrap on a crafted-magnitude balance lets a solvency or health check pass and an unbacked position be withdrawn.
Vault share pricing reads a raw contract balance shared across share classes/accounts (double-counting one deposit) and a permissionless registration path lets the attacker inject that balance.
Lending interest/index accrual uses cached elapsed-time or live totals in a way a same-block flash-loan depositor can re-trigger, harvesting accrued interest repeatedly.
Flash-loan looping/leverage helper does router.call(caller data) and trusts caller-supplied identity for Safe/module authorization, letting attackers act with permissions real users granted it.
ERC4626-style vault NAV is the unguarded live sum of underlying positions, so a same-transaction donation into a sub-vault inflates share price and lets deposit/redeem extract value.

A shared library/forwarder address intended for delegatecall or relayed use is called directly, so the downstream contract sees the shared address as msg.sender/owner and lets arbitrary callers act as it.
Initializer can be invoked again (uninitialized or weakly-guarded init), letting an attacker re-initialize a funded account/proxy with their own owner or bootstrap.
Per-address deposit/first-time incentive paid out immediately with no net against principal, farmed by cycling fresh addresses with the same capital.
